# Story 2 Behavioural Parity Checklist: PR Agent Consolidation & Portability

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of User Story 2 (FR-005 through FR-019) before/during PR review of its implementation — validates that the *requirements* are complete, clear, consistent, measurable, and cover the right scenarios, not whether any code works.
**Created**: 2026-09-21
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) — User Story 2, "The agent's PR-creation behaviour matches what's already been validated in practice"

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is "generated/compiled/lock/snapshot/translation content" (the review-budget exclusion list in FR-008) defined with specific file patterns or extensions, or left to implementer interpretation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the spec define how the agent determines whether CodeRabbit (or equivalent AI-review automation) is "enabled in the target repository" for FR-009's gate? [Gap, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK003 Does the spec define how the agent determines whether a "Linear/Asana integration tool is available" for FR-016's warn-not-fail branch? [Gap, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the exact fields and format of the `## Stack` block (position, issue/epic, dependencies, review scope) specified within this spec itself, or only by reference to `ls-theme`'s `SKILL.md`? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK005 Does the spec enumerate what "every behaviour specified in `ls-theme` `SKILL.md`" (SC-003's 100% target) actually consists of, or does it rely entirely on an external, unenumerated document? [Completeness, Spec §SC-003]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is "the additive layering" of template sections (FR-010 — following the matched template verbatim, layering in only sections it lacks) specified precisely enough to determine what counts as a section the template "lacks" vs. one it has in a different form? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK007 Is "pre-flight and self-review checks" (User Story 2's own description) distinguished clearly from "the self-review gate" (FR-009) — are these the same check under two names, or two different checks? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 2]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "warns that this step needs doing manually" (FR-016) specified with where/how that warning surfaces (PR body, chat, both)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Are FR-009's "self-review gate" and the Acceptance Scenario 6's "warn, don't block" pattern for missing tooling consistent in when each applies — is the self-review gate itself ever allowed to warn-not-block, or is it strictly blocking? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, §Acceptance Scenario 6]
- [ ] CHK010 Does FR-017's "rebase layers above afterward" identify who performs that rebase — the agent, or the human developer being guided by the agent's instructions? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-017]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality (Measurability)

- [ ] CHK011 Can "matching every behaviour specified in `PR_Agent_Consolidation_Brief.md` Source B9" (the Independent Test for User Story 2) be objectively verified by a reviewer without independently re-deriving the full behaviour list from that external document? [Measurability, Spec §User Story 2 Independent Test]
- [ ] CHK012 Is Acceptance Scenario 2's "matching the two-tier thresholds already validated in `ls-theme`" measurable directly from this spec, or does it require cross-referencing the external reference implementation to confirm the exact numbers? [Measurability, Spec §Acceptance Scenario 2]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements defined for the case where a branch has zero commits ahead of its base (nothing to derive PR content from)? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK014 Are requirements defined for a `gh` CLI failure or GitHub API error/rate-limit during any FR-005–FR-019 operation? [Gap, Exception Flow]
- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements defined for what happens if the resolved base branch (FR-006) does not actually exist in the target repository (e.g. no `develop`-equivalent, and the repository's real default is neither role)? [Coverage, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements defined for a review-thread reply (FR-017) on a PR that is not part of a stack — does "fix in the owning layer" have a defined meaning for a standalone PR? [Gap, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK017 Are recovery requirements defined for a partially-completed atomic action in FR-012 (e.g. labels applied but assignee-setting fails) — is true atomicity guaranteed, or best-effort? [Gap, Non-Functional]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK018 Are requirements defined for how long the agent should wait on required-checks confirmation (FR-016) before proceeding or timing out? [Gap, Non-Functional]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK019 Is the assumption that `PR_Agent_Consolidation_Brief.md` Source B9 remains accurate and unchanged for the duration of Story 2's implementation validated, given it documents a live, external, currently-open reference PR (`ls-theme` #53) that could itself change? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK020 Are the specific sections of `ls-theme`'s `SKILL.md` that FR-005 through FR-017 each cite ("Step 1", "Step 2.5", "Step 2.10", etc.) confirmed still to exist at those same step numbers in the live reference, or could that document have been renumbered since this spec was written? [Dependency, Spec §FR-005–§FR-017]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK021 Does "never as a separate follow-up step" (FR-012's atomicity requirement) conflict with FR-013's changelog entry, which by its own text is explicitly added *after* the PR exists — i.e. is the changelog entry correctly scoped outside FR-012's atomic action, or does the wording risk being read as contradictory? [Conflict, Spec §FR-012, §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK022 Is a requirement/acceptance-criteria ID scheme established for User Story 2's six acceptance scenarios, allowing each to be traced individually to the FR(s) it verifies? [Traceability, Gap]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
